title: The Derivative is a Local Line
tagline: Zoom into any smooth curve and it becomes a straight line — its slope is the derivative
summary: Pick a curve, drag a base point, and watch two views of the same limit. A secant slider collapses the step h toward zero so the average slope converges to the instantaneous one; a zoom slider magnifies the graph until the curve visibly straightens into its tangent. The big orange secant number slides onto the blue derivative, making the definition f'(x0) = lim (f(x0+h)-f(x0))/h something you see rather than memorize — and setting up local linearity, the reason gradients can train networks.
highlights: Drag a base point along x^2, sin x, or x^3 - x and watch the tangent line rotate to match the local slope.
Shrink the secant step h toward zero and see the average slope converge onto the exact derivative, with the gap dying like h.
Zoom geometrically into the base point until the curve straightens into a line — local linearity made literal.
Read the secant slope, derivative, and their gap live as three linked numbers.
Connects to why deep learning works: near the current weights a loss looks linear, so the gradient gives a trustworthy downhill step.
